nodes.label: Challenge Loader Codebase
nodes.rationale: A community hub for creating, sharing, and playing custom Balatro challenges (and eventually jokers, decks, etc.)

nodes.label: Next.js API Routes
nodes.rationale: Next.js API routes handle everything an Express server would do — routing, auth middleware, DB queries, JSON responses, and validation — all in one process on one port with shared TypeScript types.

nodes.label: Discord OAuth Authentication
nodes.rationale: Clean OAuth2 flow with NextAuth provider; community standard for gamer-focused apps.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled JWT via jose
nodes.rationale: Actual implementation uses hand-rolled JWT via jose library, NOT NextAuth. PLAN.md originally described NextAuth but PROGRESS.md confirms jose was used instead.

nodes.label: Single Content Table Design
nodes.rationale: Extensible to jokers, decks, vouchers — just add to CHECK constraint. One table with a type discriminator and JSONB payload.

nodes.label: Bun Runtime
nodes.rationale: Bun is an official Next.js runtime. Native TypeScript, faster than Node.js (4-5x HTTP benchmarks), smaller Docker images (90MB vs 120MB), built-in .env loading, optional Bun.sql native Postgres client.

nodes.label: Plain HTTP for Mod API (Port 3001)
nodes.rationale: luasocket in LÖVE cannot do TLS. Nginx proxies plain HTTP on port 3001 to Next.js on port 3000. Only web app users need HTTPS.

nodes.label: No Auth for Mod API
nodes.rationale: The in-game mod only reads and installs public content. Authentication is only needed for web publishing.

nodes.label: Guest User Access Design
nodes.rationale: Allow users to create draft challenges without Discord authentication. Guests cannot publish. When a guest later logs in via Discord, their drafts are transferred to their account.
